versions.title: LEAKED: harbor authority knew Northpoint dock was cracked
versions.body:
A memo from the harbor authority's engineering office, dated January 6, describes "a vertical crack in pylon N-4, approx. 40 cm" and recommends closing the north dock "at the earliest opportunity".

A week later the authority announced a "scheduled maintenance" closure and told the public "nothing about the dock is unsafe".

We have published the memo in full. Read it yourself.

versions.title: Daily Record quietly rewrites its dock story
versions.body:
The Daily Record has updated its January 21 dock article to mention "a crack in one of the dock's support pylons". The new version says the crack was found during the maintenance. Our memo is dated a week before the closure.

They added the facts. They did not add an apology.

@factcheckfran Who writes the fire report though?
There's no records room on that side. It's the loading bay. I've delivered there.

versions.title: Kestrel 'electrical fire' destroyed records room, insider says
versions.body:
A source who works at Kestrel's Dock Road site says the fire "started exactly where the paper records are kept". The fire department called it electrical within the hour. Who decided that so fast?

Kestrel did not answer our questions.

comments.text: Smart meters on my street, power out on my street. Make it make sense.
My street has no smart meters and was also dark.
@skeptic_sam That's what they want you to say.
Calder Power now says a transformer failed and 14,000 homes lost power. Not 4,000, not 40,000.
Transformer. Sure. Who replaced it, and with what?
first time commenting. lights flickered here again last night.

versions.title: The blackout was a test, and 4,000 homes were the lab
versions.body:
Calder Power says a squirrel. We say look at the map. The streets that went dark on Tuesday are the same streets that got new smart meters in December. About 4,000 homes.

A grid that can be switched off street by street is a grid that can be tested street by street. We definately expect more "squirrels".

comments.text: That pump has been running since August. Ask anyone on Mill Lane.
A pump isn't proof of anything. What was in the water?
Wait for the 'inconclusive' result. Calling it now.

versions.title: Calder Creek: dead fish downstream of a building site
versions.body:
The dead fish were found below the Route 9 bridge. Upstream, a building site has been pumping water into a drainage ditch for a month. A reader sent us photos of the pump and the grey water.

The state says algae. We say: test the ditch.

versions.title: Creek samples 'damaged in transport'. Of course they were.
versions.body:
The state lab says two of its Calder Creek samples were damaged on the way to the lab and won't be tested again. Its conclusion: "inconclusive".

We asked which samples. They would not say. We asked who transported them. They would not say. We'll keep asking.

versions.title: 'Record crowd'? Our photo says otherwise
versions.body:
The Daily Record says 9,000 people came to the Harbor Festival. Here's what Pier 2 actually looked like. [Photo: Pier 2]

We count maybe 3,000, generously. Why inflate a festival? Ask who sponsors it.

versions.title: Leaked: transit authority knew about 14 bus brake faults
versions.body:
An internal maintenance log shows that three of the six buses on route 14 had "brake response warnings" in January. Two were still in service in March.

We have published the log. The transit authority says the warnings were "sensor faults, not brake faults".

versions.title: Council's 'secret' parking plan is a spreadsheet anyone could read
versions.body: A spreadsheet on the city's own server lists 400 parking spaces in Eastfield "to be removed 2026–2028". Nobody voted on it. It was not hidden; it was just never mentioned.

versions.title: Library cut was decided before the public meeting, emails show
versions.body: Emails between two council staffers, dated a week before the public meeting on library hours, refer to the cut as "done". The council says the emails discuss "a draft".

versions.title: Water main 'accident' came two days after contract renewal
versions.body: A reader points out that the city renewed its pipe maintenance contract on March 8. The main burst on March 10. Coincidence? Probably. But someone should ask.

versions.title: Water main: questions about the contract renewal
versions.body:
A reader points out that the city renewed its pipe maintenance contract on March 8. The main burst on March 10.

We asked the city who holds the contract. We are still waiting.

versions.title: Who is buying Harbor Street?
versions.body:
Three buildings on Harbor Street have changed hands since November, including the one that houses Salty's Fish Bar. All three buyers are companies registered at the same virtual office address on Dock Road.

We're not saying what it means. We're saying it's the same address.

versions.title: 'We were told to say the call came from inside the school'
versions.body: A school employee says staff were told to describe last week's lockdown call as coming "from a number inside the district". Police say the number no longer exists. Both things can be true. Neither is reassuring.

versions.title: Ex-transit driver: 'the ghost buses were never a glitch'
versions.body: A former driver says the transit tracker shows scheduled buses as "running" whether or not a driver is available. "It looks better on the map." The authority calls it a data feed problem.

versions.title: Why are there so many new accounts praising the same lamp?
versions.body: We counted 212 reviews of the GlowNest lamp posted in one week, most from accounts less than a month old. Many use the same phrase: "my best sleep in years". We tried to buy the lamp from three shops. None had it in stock. None had ever had it in stock.

versions.title: The fog machines at the harbor
versions.body: Readers keep sending us photos of "fog machines" on the north pier. We went and looked. They are steam vents from the old cannery boiler. We're printing this so you stop sending them.

versions.title: Lights over the harbor: what we know
versions.body: Dozens of readers saw slow white lights over the harbor on January 29 last year and again on December 12. The airport says drones. The drone club says not theirs. We don't know. That's the honest answer.

versions.title: Your new doorbell is a city camera with extra steps
versions.body: Smart doorbells now cover most front doors on some Eastfield streets. Police can ask for footage without a warrant if the owner agrees. Most owners never read the box.

versions.title: The bike lane that keeps getting delayed
versions.body: The Route 9 bike lane has been "next year" since 2021. We read four years of council minutes. Every delay was voted through without debate.

versions.title: The Daily Record is a press release with a crossword
versions.body: I worked as a stringer for the Daily Record for three years. I never once saw a story spiked for being wrong. I saw plenty spiked for being inconvenient.

versions.title: Nobody you meet online is who they say. Including us?
versions.body: Readers ask if Unfiltered is real people. Fair question. Here's our answer: read the documents, not the writers. If you can check it, it doesn't matter who we are.

versions.title: Reader tip: the 6:10 ferry has a new captain nobody has met
versions.body: Several readers say the captain on the 6:10 ferry never leaves the wheelhouse and never answers a wave. The ferry company says the captain is "new and shy". We'll take their word for it, for now.

versions.title: Reader tip: free Wi-Fi at the harbor asks for a lot
versions.body: The new free Wi-Fi at Pier 2 asks for your name, email, phone number and date of birth. We read the terms: your data "may be shared with partners". The partners are not named.

versions.title: Eastfield man says he got a text from his dead brother
versions.body: An Eastfield man showed us a text that arrived on his brother's birthday from his brother's old number, two years after the funeral. The number had been given to a new customer, the phone company says. "It said 'miss you'," the man said. "Who sends that to a stranger?"

versions.title: Three people, one face: the realtors of Port Calder
versions.body: Three different estate agents in Port Calder use profile photos that are, as far as we can tell, the same man with three haircuts. Two of the agencies did not answer. The third hung up.

versions.title: Seagull attacks up 300%, and nobody is talking about it
versions.body: Four seagull attacks were reported at the harbor in February, up from one last year. Lock up your chips.
